chapter_theme: Worship of the guru, Nandi: outer worship with sandal and flowers does not reach the Lord, while inner worship in knowledge, in the place beyond sun and moon and beyond day and night, is the great worship.
structure_note: Praise of Nandi's feet opens (1847); outer offerings are set against inner knowing (1848, 1849); a verse on the daily name (1850) and one on the ranking of offerings (1851); then the place beyond sun and moon (1852, 1853), the yogic inner worship (1854) and the worship beyond day and night (1855, 1856).

1847.reading: Holding to the lotus feet of Nandi, I praise the worship that honours the teaching he gives, and the splendour that rises above the six-and-six supports.
1847.nuance: போகின்றுபதேசம் is read as போகின்ற உபதேசம், the teaching that goes forth. ஆதாரம் ஆறாறு can be the six bodily supports (adharas) or six times six, the thirty-six tattvas; either way the splendour is above them.

1848.reading: Though one worships with ten million loads of fragrant forest sandal and great flowers heaped to the sky, the one with honey-filled flowered tresses cannot be reached except by those who put away the flesh and perceive.
1848.nuance: தேனமர் பூங்குழல் names the goddess by her hair; whether she stands here for Shakti alone or for the Lord with her is not said. ஊனினை நீக்கி is usually taken as leaving identification with the body rather than abstaining from meat. Sengalvaraya cites Appar's 'ஊனையே கழிக்கவேண்டில்' for the same thought.

1849.reading: If one rises high in the knowledge one has reached, the true Supreme is there; standing in the path of knowledge is the true offering, ceaseless inner worship is the best, and reaching the red feet is the ceasing of one's own acts.
1849.nuance: The verse redefines archana (அர்ச்சனை) as standing in knowledge, not as an outer rite. செயலறல், the end of acting, is traditionally the stillness in which the soul no longer claims its acts.

1850.reading: Long for the Lord at noon, morning and evening; longing, sow his name with 'nama'; sow it, and long for him in the three spreading lights, and Nandi, the great one, will become your master.
1850.nuance: நச்சுமின் (long for) and விச்சுமின் (sow, from வித்து) alternate through the verse. Naming the Lord with நம is taken as the five-letter mantra. The three lights are usually sun, moon and fire, which yogic readings place in the body.

1851.reading: Worship in a holy mandala counts a hundredfold, worship of a fashioned image a thousandfold, and alms given to the countless ten-millionfold; but food prepared for a jnani, if you consider it, is beyond all these.
1851.nuance: பூசைநா றாகுமாம் is read as பூசை நூறு. எண்ணிலிக்கு ஐயம் may be alms to countless people or to one of countless worth. The verse ranks offerings by merit and puts feeding a knower of Siva at the top, as the next chapter will at length.

1852.reading: All worship offered in the place where moon and sun shine goes to the asuras as their share; worship in the place where moon and sun do not shine is the great worship of Nandi.
1852.nuance: Plainly read, worship done in the light of day and night is lost and worship beyond them is true. In yogic tradition moon and sun are the left and right breath channels, and the place where they do not shine is the central channel or the crown above them. Both readings stand.

1853.reading: What rises as moon and sun becomes bindu and nada in the canopy above; there, with thought gone beyond waking, worship Nandi, and that is good worship.
1853.nuance: மீதானம் (the canopy above) is traditionally the space at the crown of the head. சாக்கிராதீதம் is the state beyond waking in Siddhanta's scheme of states. The verse turns the moon and sun of 1852 into bindu and nada.

1854.reading: Turning mind and breath back at the root, making the impermanent body into its elements and setting it aside, entering the Pure One's grace and staying in bliss: this solitary worship is Sadasiva's.
1854.nuance: மனபவனம் is mind and breath, and மூலம் the root support at the base of the spine. உடல் பூதமாக்கி அகற்றி is taken as the rite of purifying the elements, in which the body is dissolved in thought before worship.

1855.reading: Worship practised by day and night becomes paired flowers for the Lord as he is by nature; worship not practised by day and night the one of hanging matted hair takes wholly.
1855.nuance: The second half may mean worship that is not bound to times, or worship in the state where day and night (the two breaths, or waking and sleep) have ceased. இணைமலர் may also be the Lord's paired feet.

1856.reading: Staying in the place where night and day are not, drinking without distraction the clear honey of bliss, in the joy of the Lord's feet where there is no night or day, I have set the night and day of maya in their two places.
1856.nuance: இராப்பகல் அற்ற இடம் is the place beyond the alternation of states. The last line is obscure: it may mean the speaker has left maya's day and night behind, or holds them apart while staying between.

links.note: 1852 says worship belongs where moon and sun do not shine; 1853 says what moon and sun become there, bindu and nada, and where the worship is done.
1855 says the Lord takes the worship not done by day and night; 1856 speaks from that place, where night and day are not and the worship is drinking bliss.

Tirumanthiram 1848 says that however much sandal and flowers one offers, she is reached only by those who put away the flesh and perceive (ஊனினை நீக்கி உணர்பவர்க்கு அல்லது). 724 says that if the body perishes the life perishes and true knowledge cannot be attained, so the poet nurtured the body (உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன்). The conflict holds only if ஊனினை நீக்கி is read as leaving the body; on the usual reading, giving up identification with it, the two can stand together.

Tirumanthiram 1845 says that at the first initiation one's own acting ceases (தன்செயல் அற்றிடும்). 1849 redefines worship as standing in knowledge and ends that reaching the red feet is the ceasing of acts (சேவடி சேரல் செயலறல் தானே). The ceasing that 1845 places at the first stage of initiation, 1849 makes the goal of inner worship itself.

Tirumanthiram 1850 bids one long for the Lord at noon, morning and evening and sow his name with 'nama' (நமவென்று நாமத்தை விச்சுமின்). 993 says the gods, showering flowers, draw near and saying 'nama' with the name (நமஎன்று நாமத்தை) stand merged with it. Both make the name joined to நம the act of worship; 1850 gives it as daily practice for people, 993 as what the gods do.

Tirumanthiram 1852 says worship in the place where moon and sun shine goes to the asuras, and worship where moon and sun do not shine (இந்துவும் பானுவும் இலங்காத் தலம்) is Nandi's great worship. 1989 says to worship when moon and sun come together (சந்திரன் சூரியன் தான்வரின் பூசனை), and those clear in the place of the two become Siva. On the yogic reading both place true worship where the two breaths cease to run apart; on a plain reading they would conflict.

Tirumanthiram 1854 describes the solitary worship of Sadasiva: turning mind and breath back at the root, making the body into its elements and setting it aside (உடல்பூதமாக்கி அகற்றி), and entering grace. 597 defines dharana as placing the dissolved body in the five elements (அரித்த உடலைஐம் பூதத்தில் வைத்து) and those in the subtle ones, held with the Supreme. The same dissolving of the body into the elements is yoga in 597 and worship in 1854.

source_issues: 1851: பூசைநா றாகுமாம் is presumably பூசை நூறு ஆகுமாம்.
1847: போகின்றுபதேசம் is read as போகின்ற உபதேசம்; the division is uncertain.
